assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets, together with dynamic models of industry, changed empirical industrial organisation. They are now standard in merger review, antitrust, trade and environmental analysis. The conceptual and methodological contribution is deep and has had broad influence across fields.
assessment.attribution: The BLP random-coefficients demand framework is clearly Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Pakes also contributed dynamic-oligopoly and productivity-estimation work (Ericson-Pakes, Olley-Pakes). Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are important but more clearly secondary or adjacent to this core, so I leave them out of the trio.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from 1994-1995 and have had three decades of validation and widespread use. The contribution is well tested and mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to include Bresnahan for the new empirical IO programme.
The relative weight of the demand-estimation and dynamic-model strands.
Whether the economics-wide significance outweighs the field's specialised character.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors built the modern theoretical and empirical framework for political economics. It covers how electoral rules and constitutions shape fiscal policy, redistribution, public goods provision and state capacity. The work links formal models to comparative evidence and influenced both economics and political science. I am a political scientist, so I applied the common criteria strictly rather than relying on field familiarity.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are credited as joint originators of the constitutional and electoral-rule agenda. Besley is credited for the state-capacity and political-agency work, with Persson on state capacity. The trio is coherent and attribution is reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from the 1990s and 2000s and has been widely replicated and extended. Recognition is ripe. A recent prize on institutions and prosperity is adjacent but addresses a different contribution.
uncertainties: Some constitutional-effects findings rest on cross-country identification that is debated.
Overlap with the recently recognised institutions literature may affect committee appetite.
Whether Besley's or other co-authors' contributions would be weighted differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles model shows how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is a cornerstone of macro-finance, and the post-2008 financial-crisis literature builds on it. It has deep theoretical influence and policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the identifiable core contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand, and some of that credit was recognised by the 2022 prize. I limit the proposal to the two cleanest originators of the collateral-constraint mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, including post-crisis reaffirmation. Mature.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the financial-accelerator work already recognised in 2022.
Whether the committee wants to include Gertler.
The balance between theory and direct empirical confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Grossman and Helpman developed political-economy models of trade protection (the 'Protection for Sale' framework). They also contributed to endogenous growth in the open economy and to the trade-and-innovation literature. The work is foundational and has been influential in both theory and empirical applications.
assessment.attribution: The pairing is natural and long-standing, with a joint body of work over decades. Credit is clear and mutual.
assessment.maturity: The central work dates from the 1990s and is mature and widely taught. The committee might also weigh the separate firm-heterogeneity strand, in which Helpman is also credited.
uncertainties: Competition from other trade-related ideas (heterogeneous firms, quantitative trade).
How much weight the committee gives special-interest politics, which has seen less empirical validation than the growth work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Together they developed the empirical optimal-taxation approach built on taxable-income elasticities and sufficient statistics. It connects theory to administrative data and has been influential in policy. The impact on public finance is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod is credited for the early taxable-income and tax-avoidance work, Saez for the elasticity and optimal-tax synthesis, and Chetty for the sufficient-statistics approach. Chetty and Saez appear in other candidates, so credit is spread across several strands and the trio is somewhat artificial.
assessment.maturity: Largely a 1990s-2010s body of work, with the more recent portion still maturing. Reasonably confirmed but still evolving.
uncertainties: Overlap with the mobility and inequality candidates affects attribution.
Whether the committee prefers a different trio or an older foundation such as Feldstein, who is no longer living.
Robustness of elasticity estimates across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification reframed empirical inference by asking what can be learned under credible, weak assumptions. It has methodological significance across applied microeconomics, policy analysis and econometrics.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator of the approach. Tamer contributed foundational results on moment inequalities and set inference in games. Molinari's contributions are important, but I limit the proposal to the strongest pair.
assessment.maturity: Manski's work dates from the late 1980s and has gradually gained acceptance. The inferential theory matured in the 2000s and 2010s. Adoption in applied work is still uneven.
uncertainties: Applied uptake is narrower than for other econometric methods.
Competing econometric candidates with wider use.
Whether Molinari should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the empirical work on trade-shock exposure changed how economists and policymakers think about labour-market polarisation and regional adjustment. Public and academic influence has been high.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz are central to the skill-biased-change and task framework. Autor, Hanson and Dorn are central to the China-shock evidence. Attribution is split across two strands, and several other contributors (such as Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane) lie outside this list.
assessment.maturity: The task-based work is about two decades old. The China-shock work is roughly a decade old and still debated.
uncertainties: Debate about the size and persistence of trade-shock effects.
Fragmented attribution between the technology and trade strands.
Recency relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, together with the rule-based analysis of monetary policy, underpins modern central-bank practice. The influence on policy and macroeconomic theory has been very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely distributed over Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler, Smets and others. Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors, which is a major difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of use. Post-pandemic inflation experience prompted renewed scrutiny of parts of the framework.
uncertainties: Difficulty of selecting a defensible trio from many contributors.
Questions about the framework's performance during the inflation surge.
Prior macroeconomics recognition may reduce appetite.
